title: Design logging and monitoring activities: decision comparison 1
teachingQuestion: How does telemetry become an owned actionable alert?
focalInsight: Definitions, decision owner/criterion, failure consequence, and retrieval remain distinct.
caption: Compare meaning, decision conditions, and failures. These concise distinctions are paired with the worked examples in the teaching unit.

nodes.label: Security Logging
nodes.definition: Logging: preserve events for later evidence
nodes.detail: Logging: preserve events for later evidence

altSummary: Definitions, decision owner/criterion, failure consequence, and retrieval remain distinct.
textFallback:
security logging: Logging: preserve events for later evidence. Decision: decide source/context/retention.. Failure/example: no record of privileged action.
monitoring: Monitoring: interpret signals for action. Decision: decide baseline/rule/owner.. Failure/example: alert queue unowned.
telemetry: Telemetry: normalized security/operational data. Decision: decide quality/coverage.. Failure/example: incompatible fields prevent correlation.
log integrity: Integrity: protect source/transport/storage. Decision: decide tamper response.. Failure/example: compromised admin erases trail.
time synchronization: Time: comparable timestamps. Decision: decide clock health.. Failure/example: correlation order wrong.
alert triage: Triage: validate/enrich/priority/route alert. Decision: decide confidence and impact.. Failure/example: true attack suppressed.
egress monitoring: Egress: detect unusual outbound movement. Decision: decide destinations/thresholds.. Failure/example: data theft unseen.
